name: uv_corner_transfer
description: What the reference editor writes into a PER-CORNER UV map when an operation rebuilds the face array (loop slice, edge bevel, face extrude, face bevel). The fixture mesh is a flat grid in z=0 whose UV is deliberately QUADRATIC in position (u = 0.10 + 0.30x + 0.40x^2, v = 0.05 + 0.20y + 0.50y^2), so 'interpolate along the edge' and 're-evaluate a planar projection at the new position' produce different numbers and the capture can tell them apart. Corners are identified by their vertex POSITION, not by index -- the operations renumber both faces and corners.
source: Frozen reference-editor capture (task 0682). Measured, not inferred: every law below was read back from the reference's own map storage after the operation, at three or more parameter values where a single value could not separate the candidates.

provenance.harness: private capture harness, uv_dump.py + t0682_uvcap.py: raw-mesh build, explicit per-corner and per-vertex UV authoring, one fresh headless boot per case, tool attributes reset to factory before every run
provenance.notes: vibe3d's loop-slice / bevel / extrude do not touch the UV plane at all today, so this fixture is NEW target behaviour, not a regression lock. The `edge_bevel_uv_seam` case records reference behaviour that looks like a defect (the new strip collapses a seam onto one island, and the corner caps get values from neither island) -- it is frozen as MEASURED, and a port should decide deliberately whether to copy it.

classification._comment: vibe3d-side annotation (task 0697), NOT part of the capture above. One entry per behaviour we deliberately do not reproduce; `status` is one of open (a gap we intend to close), closed (already closed, entry retired), permanent (we diverge on purpose and will not converge). tests/test_uv_carry_bevel_extrude.d reads these and refuses to run an open/closed branch for a permanent entry.

seam_strip_far_side.reference: The chamfer strip takes ONE island on BOTH of its sides -- the far side is the near island's parameterisation extrapolated ACROSS the seam (u = 4.4 at x = 0.8, continuing the right island's -1.0 per unit x).
seam_strip_far_side.vibe3d: Each side of the strip reads the island of the face it slid out of, so the far side lerps inside the LEFT island (0.66 at x = 0.8) and the seam survives the bevel.
seam_strip_far_side.why_permanent: The reference's own capture note calls this a defect (`MEASURED, NOT ENDORSED`). Reproducing it would mean deliberately collapsing a user's UV seam onto one island; a per-corner source is exactly the machinery that makes not doing so possible. There is no future in which we converge, so this is not a gap to close.

seam_corner_caps.reference: The two corner-cap triangles get values that match NEITHER island -- a similarity transform of the geometric triangle (the UV edges come out 0.98489x the geometric ones), from a construction nothing else in the capture exhibits.
seam_corner_caps.vibe3d: Each cap corner takes the edge lerp in the island of one adjacent face (f_k, the deterministic side), so every cap value belongs to a real island of the mesh.
seam_corner_caps.why_permanent: Same root as `seam_strip_far_side` and the same reasoning: no island membership at all is worse than a deterministic one, and the reference value is not reconstructible from any law the rest of this fixture pins.

cases.name: loop_slice_pos025
cases.law: Inserted vertex UV = lerp of the two endpoint UVs of the edge it split, at the same fraction as its geometric position on that edge. The UV map is quadratic in position, so re-projecting position->UV would give 0.48125 where the measured value is 0.575.

cases.name: loop_slice_pos050
cases.law: Same law at the midpoint; separates 'lerp' from 'always the midpoint' only in combination with the pos025/pos075 cases.

cases.name: loop_slice_pos075
cases.law: Third fraction; three distinct fractions pin the lerp.

cases.name: loop_slice_count3
cases.law: Three evenly spaced loops; every inserted vertex follows the same lerp.

cases.name: loop_slice_uv_seam
cases.law: The split edge lies ON a UV seam (its two adjacent faces carry different UVs at the shared vertices). Each side of the seam gets its OWN lerp, in its own island; the seam survives the slice.

cases.name: edge_bevel_offset02
cases.law: Every vertex the bevel creates lies ON an original edge; its UV = lerp of that edge's two endpoint UVs at its geometric fraction along it.

cases.name: edge_bevel_offset04
cases.law: Second offset on the same layout; the fraction tracks the offset.

cases.name: edge_bevel_nonuniform
cases.law: Incident edges of DIFFERENT lengths (1.0 and 2.0). The UV fraction is offset/edgeLength (0.1 on the length-2 edge), not the raw offset -- a uniform grid cannot tell those apart.

cases.name: edge_bevel_uv_seam
cases.law: The beveled edge IS the UV seam. MEASURED, NOT ENDORSED: the reference does NOT reproduce both islands on the new strip -- the strip takes ONE island on both of its sides (the far side extrapolated across the seam), and the two corner-cap triangles get values that match neither island.

cases.name: face_extrude_no_uv_sweep
cases.law: No UV sweep: the moved cap keeps the source face's UVs verbatim and each side wall's top corner copies its own base corner's UV, so every wall is DEGENERATE in UV (zero area).

cases.name: face_extrude_uv_sweep_u
cases.law: UV sweep along U (the reference's factory setting for this tool, active only while a UV map is the current map): the cap still keeps the source UVs, but each wall gets a FRESH parameterisation -- u=0 on the base ring, u=1 on the top ring, v = the source vertex's own v. The original u of the boundary vertices is discarded on the walls.

cases.name: face_bevel_connected
cases.law: Connected UVs (the reference's factory setting for this tool). The inset face's UV polygon is the source face's UV polygon inset by a distance of insetDistance * (uvPerimeter / geometricPerimeter) -- NOT the UV interpolated at the new geometric position.

cases.name: face_bevel_connected_nonuniform
cases.law: Non-square face: the UV inset distance is 0.384286 = 0.2 * 13.45/7, confirming the perimeter-ratio scale; the parametric reading would give 0.38 in u and 0.39 in v (different per axis) instead of one distance.

cases.name: face_bevel_connected_inset04
cases.law: Second inset on the same face: the UV inset distance scales linearly (0.64 = 0.4 * 1.6).
